answer: Persistent chained attestation anchors each new identity to a prior signed record, so copying one forces replay of its whole history. Like a glacier carving a unique valley, every agent accrues a tamper-evident trace that cannot be cloned without diverging. At its zenith the verification cost per duplicate equals replaying full storage and signature checks, not a token fee. Anchoring each chain to a distinct physical jetty (network endpoint) makes parallel duplicates collide, so the attacker pays continuous bandwidth and storage to sustain fakes.
